purpose: The by-PNU panel Gold tables (and the unit price history, root ADR-0190) the scheduled job foundation-gold-panel-rebuild.service rebuilds (orchestration/jobs.v1.json gold_panel_rebuild), in the order it rebuilds them, with each table's producer, the producer flags the job passes, the Spark size it runs at, and how many rows a rebuild may lose against the current snapshot before it is refused. The Silver inputs are the producer's own constants (root ADR-0130), not listed here. infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs/gold_rebuild.py reads this file; scripts/ops/gold-panel-rebuild.sh reads the spark sizes. `incremental` (root ADR-0180) lets a rebuild recompute only the PNUs whose inputs changed and merge them, up to max_changed_key_fraction of the Gold, after a parity sample of parity_sample_keys unchanged PNUs agrees; past it, or without it, the rebuild is full.

gold.parcel_panel.max_row_loss_reason: One row per current parcel. A monthly national parcel refresh moves the count by far less than 1% (parcels split, merge or retire a few thousand at a time out of about 40 million); losing more means an input lost a region or a join broke, which must not reach the bake.

unmeasured_inputs.silver.parcel_lineage: Absent from the catalog when the parcel rebuild was measured (2026-10-03) and still absent on 2026-10-04, so the 20g cap was shown only with --no-carry-lineage, where the run already peaked at 18.0GiB anon. Carrying the lineage adds a join; measure it before a run may read it (root ADR-0139).

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180. Past 30% of the 39.9M PNUs recomputing them costs most of a full rebuild and the copy-on-write merge still copies the untouched rows of every file it touches, so the full rebuild is the cheaper commit. 20,000 unchanged PNUs (0.05%) rebuilt beside the changed ones prove the current Gold is what the build makes of its pins; they ride the same input scan.

gold.building_panel.max_row_loss_reason: One row per PNU that has a building title or unit. Building registers grow; a monthly refresh moves the count by far less than 1% of about 6 million. Losing more means an input lost a region or a join broke, which must not reach the bake.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180. Past 30% of the 5.95M PNUs recomputing them costs most of a full rebuild and the copy-on-write merge still copies the untouched rows of every file it touches, so the full rebuild is the cheaper commit. 20,000 unchanged PNUs (0.3%) rebuilt beside the changed ones prove the current Gold is what the build makes of its pins; they ride the same input scan.

gold.unit_price_panel.max_row_loss_reason: One row per PNU with a priced unit (root ADR-0190). A price vintage keeps every reference date it ever published and units are rarely removed, so a monthly refresh moves the count by far less than 1%; losing more means a vintage lost a region or the unit join broke, which must not reach the bake.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180, as for the building panel. A monthly vintage changes the prices of few units, so its PNUs are recomputed and merged; a new reference date a year changes most priced PNUs and runs the full rebuild, which is then the cheaper commit.

gold.unit_price_panel.max_price_history_shrink_reason: A price vintage keeps every reference date it ever published (root ADR-0185), so a unit's price history only grows; a unit loses records only when its register is retired, a few at a time. On 2026-10-11 a vintage loaded in part made a Gold in which 47,153 units had lost about 65% of their records (not served only because that day's bake failed). The producer refuses, before it writes, a Gold in which more than 0.1% of the current Gold's units keep fewer records or none.

pins_from.reason: Root ADR-0190. A unit's price is served under the PNU its building document carries it, so both documents must place each unit from the same register snapshots: a unit relinked to another title between two separate pins would be under one PNU in the building document and another in the price document. The rebuild pins these inputs to the snapshots the current building Gold was built from (it runs after the building panel in `all`), never to their heads.

gold.parcel_zoning.max_row_loss_reason: One row per served parcel with a zoning verdict (root ADR-0193), a subset of the parcel panel's rows. A land use plan vintage moves the zoned parcels by far less than 1% of them; losing more means a vintage lost a region or the anchor walk broke, which must not reach the bake.

unmeasured_inputs.silver.parcel_lineage: As for gold.parcel_panel: no run carrying the lineage was measured, and this table's inputs are pinned to the panel's, which has none.

incremental.reason: Root ADR-0180, as for the parcel panel. A land use plan vintage reaches the PNUs it zones; a zone code table change is a whole-table input and rebuilds whole (the producer's WHOLE_TABLE_INPUTS).

pins_from.reason: Root ADR-0193 §3 and §6-2. While gold.parcel_panel is what the web reads, this table is that panel's zonings section: every input is pinned to the snapshots the current panel was built from, so a served PNU is never alive in one lane and retired in the other, and every full rebuild checks its verdicts against the panel's on every PNU before it writes. Last in `all`, after the panel it follows: its first build (a full one) cannot hold the building tables past the job's timeout. When the zoning lane becomes the reference (the panel retires) this entry is removed.
